title: Dependability alignment — sprint ledger and milestone plan (2026)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sprint-ledger for a cross-functional dependability program focused on regularizing Service Level Objectives (SLOs), aligning engineering teams on observability and incident handling, and establishing a repeatable rollout cadence for SLO adoption across product areas.

Why a sprint-ledger?
- Avoid a single monolithic project plan — ledger keeps short, verifiable sprint outcomes and makes cross-team dependencies visible.
- Emphasize small increments: define, instrument, validate, operate.
- Prioritize measurable signals and short feedback loops.

Scope and boundaries:
- Surface area: platform infra, API surface (hosted Redwood API), Dedicated routing, and Console alerting hooks.
- Includes SLO definition templates, monitoring dashboards, alert runbooks, and cross-team onboarding (platform, serving-runtime, console, product-hosted-api).
- Excludes long-run changes to model serving kernels (those will be owned by serving-runtime and tracked as dependent work).

High-level objectives (OKRs):
- O1: Roll out baseline availability and latency SLOs for 5 core services by end of Q2 with verified measurement (end-to-end).
- O2: Reduce alert noise by 45% via improved SLIs and alert thresholds and runbook-based deduping.
- O3: Document and train 3 cross-functional playbooks: SLO onboarding, Canary verification, and Emergency rollback.

Success metrics (how we know we succeeded):
- SLO coverage: % of services with defined, instrumented, and monitored SLOs (target 80% for prioritized list).
- Alert reduction: alerts per-service/per-week baseline vs post-rollout (target -45%).
- Time-to-detect/resolve (TTD/MTTR) for SLI regressions (target TTD <= 5m for high-severity signals).
- Postmortem quality: all Sev2+ incidents have an owner and remediation action within 7 days.

Sprint ledger (6 two-week sprints, ledger rows show sprint focus, acceptance):
- Sprint A (2026-03-08 to 2026-03-19): Prioritize service list + canonical SLI definitions.
  - Owner: Maya Chen / Owen Ramirez.
  - Deliverables: prioritized service roster (5 core services), SLI templates (availability, p50/p95 latency, error_budget burn rate), instrumentation checklist.
  - Acceptance: roster + templates in Confluence; two pilot services commit to instrumentation.

- Sprint B (2026-03-22 to 2026-04-02): Instrumentation and data sanity checks for pilots.
  - Owner: Service owners (product-hosted-api lead) + infra SREs.
  - Deliverables: dashboards for pilots, sample SLO report, canonical dashboard panels.
  - Acceptance: dashboards show stable SLI time-series over 48h; CI jobs to surface metric gaps.

- Sprint C (2026-04-05 to 2026-04-16): Alert shaping + runbook authoring; draft canary verification steps.
  - Owner: Leo Fischer / Priya Desai.
  - Deliverables: alert rules mapped to SLO thresholds, runbook skeleton, canary checklist.
  - Acceptance: alert noise baseline measured; runbook pages created and linked from alert actions.

- Sprint D (2026-04-19 to 2026-04-30): Cross-team verification & tabletop exercises.
  - Owner: SRE leads and Product PMs.
  - Deliverables: 2 tabletop exercises (one backend latency, one deployment failure), adjustments to runbooks.
  - Acceptance: post-exercise action list closed or scheduled; signoff from involved product teams.

- Sprint E (2026-05-03 to 2026-05-14): Canary rollout of SLO enforcement (soft alerts + dashboarding for 5 services).
  - Owner: Platform Eng + Console team.
  - Deliverables: canary traffic routing for non-critical customers, dashboarding templates exported, training session scheduled.
  - Acceptance: no regression in latency/availability for canary tenants; feedback collected.

- Sprint F (2026-05-17 to 2026-05-28): Full rollout & retrospective; finalize guardrails.
  - Owner: Maya Chen / SRE leadership.
  - Deliverables: SLO adoption checklist, rollout report, noise reduction summary, playbooks finalized.
  - Acceptance: adoption checklist signed by owners; retrospective documented with 3 improvement actions.

Cross-functional roles & RACI (simplified):
- Eng-SRE: lead measurement, alerting, runbooks (Responsible).
- Platform Eng: provide routing/canary infra and quota controls (Accountable).
- Product teams (hosted API, dedicated): provide service owners, define customer impact model (Responsible/Consulted).
- Console + Observability: create dashboards and user-facing SLO views (Responsible).
- Applied-ML / Serving-runtime: consult on model-related latency modes; provide compatible SLI exports (Consulted).
- Solutions Eng / CS: help with onboarding key customers to canary programs (Informed).

Instrumenting SLIs (notes & constraints):
- Prefer end-to-end user-centric SLIs over internal queues for availability. Example: "user request success rate (>=200ms) measured at API gateway".
- Latency buckets: p50, p95, p99. For SLOs we target p95/p99 depending on endpoint criticality.
- Error definition: include 5xx and model misbehaviors where model output violates schema (tracked as structured validation failure).
- Sampling/volume constraints: large-scale batching endpoints will require statistical extrapolation; note in instrumentation checklist.

Alerting philosophy (short):
- Alerts should be for actionable events; prefer symptom-based alerts tied to SLO burn rather than raw metric thresholds except for safety signals.
- Tiering: page for high-severity SLO burns (>= X% error budget in 30m window), notify channel for medium severity, log alert for low-severity.
- Deduping: route alerts to a central enrichment service before paging to strip duplicates. (Tech spike required).

Runbook / Playbook outlines (to be filled per service):
- Incident summary & immediate mitigation steps.
- How to check SLI dashboards & key panels.
- Canary rollback steps (traffic reroute commands), owner contact list, escalation path.
- Postmortem template & remediation tracking link.

Communication & training plan:
- Weekly 30m sync (Wednesdays 10:00) during sprints A–D for status and blockers.
- Two-hour workshop during Sprint D for tabletop exercises (mandatory for product owners).
- Short recorded walkthroughs for console views and SLO pages.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Metric gaps for legacy services -> Mitigation: fallback SLO using proxy metrics + flag for re-instrumentation backlog.
- Risk: Alert fatigue -> Mitigation: conservative paging rules in canary and iterative tightening.
- Risk: Overly strict SLOs cause release blocking -> Mitigation: soft enforcement window + auto-fallback to previous model variant.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Define exact error budget policy for model-related semantic failures — does product own severity mapping? (Action: Priya to propose by Sprint A end).
- Who funds dedicated observability retention increases (for long-tail SLI storage)? Finance & infra alignment needed.

Action items (first 10):
- Maya: finalize prioritized service roster (due 2026-03-05).
- Owen: publish SLI templates in Confluence and open instrumentation checklist PR (due 2026-03-12).
- Priya: draft error-budget mapping proposal (due 2026-03-12).
- Leo: spike alert enrichment dedupe service feasibility (due 2026-03-19).
- Ana: schedule Sprint D tabletop; create invite list and scenarios (due 2026-04-02).

Notes-to-self / fragile bits:
- Keep runbooks short. We iterate with 1-pager + checklist.
- Watch for API gateway sampling bias when measuring user-facing latency.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: REL-DEPEND-INIT (linked above).
- Jira board: JIRA-REL-678 for backlog items.
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421 (canary routing).

If you're reading this and want to contribute: add your name to collaborators, comment inline on the sprint acceptance criteria, and flag any missing dependencies.

-- end of ledger (working draft)
